pr_title: Add link to not deprecated modules docs
pr_body:
closes: #14394

I was only able to link python classes that are defined in `apache-airflow`.

Not sure how to link them with classes that are defined in providers.
pr_comments:
> Not sure how to link them with classes that are defined in providers.

It should work normally e.g. ``:class:`airflow.providers.google.cloud.operators.kubernetes_engine` `` See also: https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/master/docs/apache-airflow/concepts.rst#operators (operators section)
Accidentally edited another commit with amend.

issue_context.title: Add link to not deprecated modules docs
issue_context.body:
There are a lot of documentation that is the first link when you google something that actually doesn't contain anything because of the update of the paths. 

For instance, if you google `trigger dagrun operator` the first link is https://airflow.apache.org/docs/apache-airflow/stable/_api/airflow/operators/dagrun_operator/index.html
Which has the following content:
![Captura de pantalla 2021-02-23 a las 16 25 38](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11339132/108865688-c5257080-75f3-11eb-9676-323efbe29f42.png)

The ideal situation would be that the google search brings you to the correct link, but otherwise, it would be nice to have at least a link to the new module in the same page
comments: This is a good idea and can be assigned to me

review_comments:
```suggestion
"""This module is deprecated. Please use :mod:`airflow.sensors.filesystem`."""
```

Since this is a module and not class, same for all other cases too

Docs for it: https://www.sphinx-doc.org/en/master/usage/restructuredtext/domains.html#cross-referencing-python-objects

The default language is `python` so you can use `:py:mod:` or just `:mod:`
I didn't realize they were referencing modules. I'll use that!
